"You all have 72 hours to acquire as many points as you can, and by the end of the examination, the five disciples with the most points will become Inner Court disciples."
"All participants will be provided with a Spirit-grade weapon of their choosing, and you are forbidden from using anything that wasn't provided to you.
This includes medicine, such as recovery pills and strengthening pills.
Any questions?"
When nobody responded, the sect elder handed everyone a weapon of their choosing before announcing, "Then I will officially begin the examination now.
Good luck, everyone."
The moment the examination began, every participant—except for Yuan—immediately rushed into the examination area, eager to prove themselves.
The area itself was vast, resembling the Hunting Grounds with its dense forests, rugged terrain, and lurking dangers.
"What are you waiting for?" Elder Sun asked Yuan.
"Nothing.
I'll see you soon."
Yuan said before entering the area the next moment.
After entering the examination area, Yuan immediately used his Divine Sense to survey his surroundings.
'I can see a few Spirit Master-level magical beasts between the third and sixth level nearby, but they only have a green ribbon.'
Yuan encountered his first magical beast with a red ribbon, and it was at the eighth level of Spirit Master.
Most of the participants for the examination were far beyond the first level of Spirit Master, with many of them between the seventh level and even the peak of Spirit Master.
However, even then, most of them only fought beasts weaker than their own cultivation.
As for Yuan, he ignored every single magical beast he encountered to find the beast with a black ribbon.
Of course, he wasn't the only one who thought of this strategy, as several other disciples wanted to go straight for the black ribbon.
After several hours of moving without stopping, Yuan finally encountered the beast with a black ribbon.
It was a magical beast with cultivation at the 3rd level of Spirit Grandmaster.
However, he was not the first to find it, as there was already someone fighting it.
This disciple was at the first level of Spirit Grandmaster, and he was struggling against the beast.
It was clear that this disciple did not have the capability to defeat it.
Seeing this, instead of waiting for the disciple to meet his inevitable defeat, Yuan joined the fight and, with a single devastating strike, decapitated the beast.
"W-What?!" The disciple who was fighting the beast was shocked, to say the least.
Of course, he was also angry that someone had the audacity to steal his kill.
"You bastard!
Didn't you see I was already fighting that beast?!
How dare you steal my kill?!"
Yuan picked up the black ribbon and turned to look at the disciple.
"Yes, I saw, and it was clear that you wouldn't have defeated it.
Instead of cursing at me, you should be thanking me for helping you save time and energy.
If you start hunting seriously, you might catch up to the others," Yuan said before turning away.
"Where do you think you're going with my black ribbon?!" The disciple quickly stopped him from leaving by blocking his path.

chapters.title: Chapter 1894 Passing the Examination
paragraphs: "Your black ribbon?" Yuan turned to face the disciple with amusement.
"Y-Yeah! If I hadn't distracted that magical beast, you wouldn't have been able to defeat it!" the disciple blurted out, his voice slightly unsteady.
Despite his confident-sounding words, there was no conviction in his tone. It was clear—even to himself—that he didn't truly believe what he was saying.
"What an amusing thing to say. Alright. If you truly think you deserve this black ribbon, come get it from me." Yuan extended the ribbon toward the disciple.
"S-Seriously?" The disciple asked with a doubtful gaze.
Yuan smiled and responded, "Of course, I am being serious. However, I won't be giving it to you without a fight."
"You—!" The disciple immediately realized what Yuan was trying to do and halted his movements.
Yuan continued, "There's no rule saying the participants can't steal other participants' ribbons. If you really want this ribbon, come steal it from me."

The disciple was speechless. He knew he stood no chance against Yuan, who defeated the magical beast in a single strike. He also knew that Yuan would've been able to do the same thing even if he wasn't distracting it.
Without saying another word, the disciple turned around and quickly left the scene.

Shortly after the disciple left, instead of leaving himself, Yuan turned toward a certain direction and spoke out loud, "This goes for you guys, too. If you think you have what it takes to take the black ribbon from me, I welcome you to try!"

The participants, who had been hiding and viewing everything from a distance, were shocked when Yuan suddenly called out to them. However, none of them dared to reveal themselves, much less challenge Yuan.
"Then I'll take my leave."
Yuan left the place the next moment, immediately leaving the examination area.
"Huh? Why are you back already? There's still plenty of time left." Elder Sun was puzzled when Yuan returned so soon.
Yuan didn't say anything and showed everyone there the black ribbon.

"He actually hunted a magical beast with a black ribbon this quickly?! The last time someone managed to acquire a black ribbon was seventy years ago!" The other sect elders muttered to each other, their voices full of surprise.

The examiner approached Yuan and said, "Congratulations on passing the examination, Disciple Xiao Yang. You are an Inner Court disciple starting from this moment. You can move to the Inner Court once you find a suitable house."
"Can I stay in the Outer Court?" Yuan asked.
The examiner had never heard of anyone refusing to move to the Inner Court and was quite baffled by Yuan's question.

After snapping out of his daze, he responded, "We can't force you to move, so if that's what you want... but are you sure? The spiritual energy inside the Inner Court is much denser, which will be beneficial to your cultivation. Moreover, it won't be convenient for you when you have to travel to the Inner Court for whatever reason."
"Why do you want to stay in the Outer Court? Are you unwilling to separate from your friends or something? I expect you to visit my place for training often, you know?" Elder Sun also chimed in.
"Training, huh?"
Yuan became silent to ponder. A moment later, he nodded, "Alright, I'll move to the Inner Court."
Although he initially planned on staying in the Outer Court for the others, Yuan decided to have more trust in his companions.
'What am I even worried about? They're powerful and capable enough, and I'm sure they'll enter the Inner Court soon.'

Yuan realized he was babysitting the others too much even though they never asked for it, which could be considered as not having enough trust in them. Yuan left the examination area with Elder Sun shortly after.
"Your new uniforms will be ready in three days. In the meantime, you can look for a new home inside the Inner Court," said Elder Sun as she brought Yuan back to his living quarters.
"Get some rest for now. Come find me once you've moved into the Inner Court, and we'll immediately begin your training."
"See you later, Elder Sun."
However, instead of leaving, Elder Sun looked at Yuan with a worried face and said, "Things might get complicated and difficult for you in the Inner Court, but it'll quickly pass."
Yuan smiled and asked, "Are you referring to what I went through with those Inner Court disciples before?"
Elder Sun nodded. "Yes, you'll probably be mistaken for Tian Yang again and again."
"Who is this Tang Yang, anyway? You also mistook me for him during our first meeting. And why does it seem like he has so many enemies?"

"Tian Yang... is an Inner Court disciple who looks exactly like you. I wouldn't be surprised if you were twins. As for having a lot of enemies... Well, I can't deny that. While it's not like he goes around picking fights, he never backs down from one, even if it's a simple taunt from another disciple."
"I see. Do you think I'll be able to meet him?" Yuan then asked.
"He's currently out training for the Core Disciple examination, but he should be back in a few years."
"A few years, huh? I cannot wait."
Despite saying such words, Yuan had a feeling the two of them would not meet in this world.
Elder Sun left shortly after.
"Congratulations on passing the examination."

Xi Meili and the others greeted him with smiles the moment they saw him, offering their congratulations without even asking how it went. It was as if his success was a foregone conclusion, something so expected that there was no need for doubt. Their confidence in him was unwavering, and to them, there was never a question of if he would pass—only when.
Yuan then revealed to them that he would be moving to the Inner Court in a few days.
"I see. Don't worry about us. We'll follow you to the Inner Court soon."
"Of course." Yuan nodded with a smile.

chapters.title: Chapter 1895 Tian Yang’s Existence
paragraphs: After a day of rest, Yuan entered the Inner Court with Elder Sun's medallion to look for a new house. Of course, he already had one in mind.
Once he found a servant to assist him, Yuan went straight to Tian Yang's living quarters and asked about its availability.
The servant retrieved a jade slip and took a moment to look through its content before responding, "Sorry, but this place is already taken by another disciple."
Yuan narrowed his eyes upon hearing this and asked, "Is this disciple's name Tian Yang?"
"Yes, that is correct."
'So Tian Yang actually exists in this world... but does he physically exist?' Yuan wondered inwardly.
From the beginning, he had believed that Tian Yang was merely a fabrication of memories, a figure that only persisted in Elder Sun and the others' recollections—not a real, living person.
His reasoning had been simple: the Heaven Refining Crystal's existence.

Tian Yang, according to history, should have been the one to acquire it long before Yuan's arrival at the Immortal Monastery. Yet, it was still in the Confinement Chamber, allowing Yuan to claim it instead. That contradiction alone had led him to believe that Tian Yang was nothing more than an illusion, an existence that didn't physically exist.

Sometime later, Yuan picked a random available building as his new living quarters. After acquiring the keys to his new home, Yuan went to find Elder Sun at her peak—the 21st peak, known as the Immortal Sun Peak. Moreover, the Immortal Sun Peak hovered above the ground like a flying island.
"Hm? You're here already? Are you that eager to start your training?" Elder Sun said after seeing him.
Yuan silently nodded with an eager smile on his face. "Follow me."

Once they arrived at the training grounds, Elder Sun spoke, "Before we begin, I must be completely honest with you. As embarrassing as it sounds, especially after I spoke so highly of my qualifications, you're my first disciple, so I don't really know what to teach you."

"Of course, it's not like I don't know how to teach you. I just don't know what to teach you. That said, seeing how fast your cultivation is progressing, I probably don't have to teach you about cultivation."
"What techniques have you learned, and do you have any techniques you want to learn or have difficulty understanding?"
Yuan pondered for a moment before responding, "I know a little about the Peerless Immortal Technique and a few of the sect's sword techniques. As for what I want to learn... I don't know."
"I see... In that case, show me how far you've progressed with the Peerless Immortal Technique, as well as the other techniques."
Yuan nodded and began demonstrating 'all' of the techniques he knew.
Elder Sun was left speechless by the end.
"G-Give me a moment to think..." Elder Sun said before falling silent.

'This little monster has already mastered the second level of the Peerless Immortal Technique?! He'd only joined the sect recently!' she cried inwardly, trying to fathom how someone who'd just joined the sect could reach such a high level of understanding for one of their most difficult techniques.
'It took me almost ten years to reach that level, and I was considered one of the most talented individuals in my family!'

'As for his other techniques... while they're not as impressive as his Peerless Immortal Technique, being just slightly above average, if we consider how he probably spent most of his time studying the Peerless Immortal Technique, it's unfathomable how he got the time to learn other techniques!'
After pondering for many minutes, Elder Sun decided to focus on the other techniques Yuan was cultivating to balance out his foundations.
"Although we won't be focusing on the Peerless Immortal Technique, you can still ask me questions about it. The same goes for your cultivation. If you have any trouble, tell me about it."
"Yes, Elder Sun!" Yuan nodded with a smile.
Yuan had purposefully lowered his skills during the demonstration because he was afraid that Elder Sun might quit being his master if she thought there was nothing she could teach him.
Although he still intended to complete the trial, Yuan wanted to use this opportunity to spend as much time as he could with Elder Sun, something Tian Yang could only dream about.
Thus, Yuan began his life in the Inner Court.
In the blink of an eye, another year passed.

During this time, besides going to Elder Sun for lectures three days a week, Yuan would spend most of his time hunting magical beasts in the Hunting Grounds, completely ignoring the training areas available within the Inner Court.

These training grounds assisted the disciples in their understanding of certain techniques and cultivation, but they were useless to Yuan, who had already reached the pinnacle understanding of most techniques in the sect.

As for improving his cultivation, it was simply more effective to hunt magical beasts and consume their monster cores. With the points he'd saved from selling the beasts' materials, Yuan earned enough points to purchase a few more treasures from the point store, further improving his talent and cultivation.

Meanwhile, many of the participants in the trial gave up on trying to become first and started focusing on the Immortal Monastery's techniques after realizing they had no chance to catch up to those who had managed to purchase a treasure before they were sold out.
Since they knew they wouldn't be able to inherit everything, they decided to memorize and acquire as many techniques from the Immortal Monastery as possible to bring back to their original world.
However, many participants still continued to aim for first place. Ji Ran became the second individual to become an Inner Court disciple, entering the Inner Court four months after Yuan.
Xi Meili and the others were still Outer Court disciples, but they only lacked a contribution point or two required to take the examination.
"It's been a year since you've become an Inner Court disciple, Xiao Yang. Are you still being mistaken for Tian Yang these days?" Elder Sun suddenly asked.
Yuan shook his head and said, "Ever since I shortened my hair, they stopped messing with me."

Elder Sun looked at Yuan with his short hair and smiled, "Are you sure it's not because you're beating all of them up even at the slightest provocation? You're even more outrageous than Tian Yang in this aspect."

chapters.title: Chapter 1896 Audience With the Sect Leader
paragraphs: "Alright, show me your progress with the Peerless Immortal Technique," Elder Sun said to Yuan.
Yuan nodded and showed off his progress, which had reached the third level.
'To think he'd enter the third level of the technique after just a year of training... As I thought, his talents when it comes to comprehension are monstrous.' Elder Sun thought to herself.
"Okay, now show me your other—"
Elder Sun's words abruptly cut off, her voice trailing into silence.
Her expression suddenly changed, the light curiosity in her eyes vanishing as a serious and worried look took its place.
A sudden, almost palpable tension filled the air.

Elder Sun's brows furrowed, and her gaze sharpened, as if she had sensed something deeply unsettling. It was not just concern—it was the kind of reaction that only came when something was terribly wrong.
Noticing this, Yuan asked her, "What's the matter, Elder Sun?"
"Sorry, but let's end our training here. Something else came up."
Without explaining further, Elder Sun left the scene in a hurry, leaving Yuan to ponder what caused her to make such an expression.
'Don't tell me... Is it because of that...?' he wondered, as he had an idea what made Elder Sun leave.
After leaving the Immortal Sun Peak, Yuan wandered the Inner Court to see if any of the disciples were gossiping, and they did not disappoint.
"Did you hear? All nine Immortal Clans gathered for a meeting for the first time in decades."
"If the Nine Immortal Clan suddenly became active, something big will surely happen soon."
Hearing this information, Yuan realized the Nine Immortal Clans were planning on sealing the Desolate Continent with the Immortal Ensnaring Vault.
This meant that Elder Sun's sudden departure was most likely because the life-saving treasure she had secretly given Tian Yang had been activated, signaling that he was in danger.
'At this rate, the opening of Han Zexian's Tomb will happen in about a year...'
A few days later, Elder Sun returned.
"Sorry for suddenly leaving you like that," she apologized to him.
"There's no need to apologize. That said, I'm curious. Did something happen?" Yuan knew it was unlikely Elder Sun would tell him about the situation, but he still asked.

To his surprise, Elder Sun said with a deep sigh, "I gave Tian Yang a life-saving treasure before he left the sect, and I sensed its activation. I don't know what he's gotten himself into this time, but he's likely in a life-or-death situation."
"That doesn't sound good. Are you going to leave the sect to save him?"
Elder Sun shook her head.
"Unfortunately, I don't know where he is right now. I am only able to sense the activation of the treasure, not where it was activated from..."
Yuan fell silent for a moment before speaking, "Have you heard of a place called the Desolate Continent?"
"The Desolate Continent? Of course, it's a lawless place. Why did you bring it up?"
"Well, to be honest, I heard a few of the disciples talking about Tian Yang visiting that place."
"What?! Is that true?!" Elder Sun's eyes widened with disbelief.
Yuan calmly nodded.
"That dumb, stupid idiot!" Elder Sun stomped the ground angrily, her face full of frustration. "Of all places, why'd he go there?!"
"Now that you know where he is, are you going to help him?" Yuan then asked.
"That's... Even if I know where he is, I need to ask the Sect Leader for permission first."
"If you're going to speak with the Sect Leader, can you bring me with you? I'd like to speak with him, too."
"What? The Sect Leader isn't someone you can meet just because you want to."
"I know, but it won't hurt to ask. After all, I've already spoken to him once before."
"Okay, I'll ask him. I will let you know when he responds."
Yuan nodded.
A week later, Elder Sun revealed the Sect Leader's response to Yuan, "The Sect Leader has agreed to speak with you, but he said it'd cost you 1,000,000 points, whatever that means."
'A million points just to speak with him? That's robbery in broad daylight!' Yuan cried inwardly after hearing this.
"Okay..." He nodded.
"Then I'll bring you to speak with him in three days."
Three days later, Elder Sun and Yuan made their way to the Sect Leader's quarters.
"Wait here while I speak with the Sect Leader first," Elder Sun said to Yuan before entering the building.
Her conversation with the Sect Leader lasted only for a few minutes.
"Did you get the Sect Leader's permission to leave the sect?" Yuan asked her.
"Yes. It's your turn now. I'll wait for you."
"I'll be back."
A few moments later, Yuan entered the Sect Leader's room.
"It's you again." The Sect Leader frowned upon seeing Yuan's face. Of course, it wasn't because he disliked Yuan. It was just a natural reaction for the Sect Leader.
"What do you want? A million points will only grant you ten minutes with me."
"I have a few questions," Yuan quickly responded.
"In that case, it'll cost you an additional 100,000 points for every question."
Yuan was left speechless after hearing this, but as much as he wanted to complain, he had no qualifications to do so, as this was not his world or trial.
'After paying 1,000,000 points, I have 300,000 points left... Three questions, huh? Better make them count...' he sighed inwardly.
After a moment of silence, Yuan spoke, "For my first question, I want to know how I can leave the sect. I want to visit the Desolate Continent with Elder Sun."
The Sect Leader smiled and said, "Instead of asking if you can leave, you asked for the method, huh?"
"If you wish to leave the Immortal Monastery and start venturing outside, you must pay a one-time fee of 10,000,000 points."
Yuan's eyes widened at the astronomical amount.
"Ten million points just to leave?!" he was in disbelief.

Elder Sun's words abruptly cut off, her voice trailing into silence.
Her expression suddenly changed, the light curiosity in her eyes vanishing as a serious and worried look took its place.
A sudden, almost palpable tension filled the air.
Elder Sun's brows furrowed, and her gaze sharpened, as if she had sensed something deeply unsettling.
It was not just concern—it was the kind of reaction that only came when something was terribly wrong.
Noticing this, Yuan asked her, "What's the matter, Elder Sun?"
"Sorry, but let's end our training here.
Something else came up."
Without explaining further, Elder Sun left the scene in a hurry, leaving Yuan to ponder what caused her to make such an expression.
'Don't tell me...
Is it because of that...?' he wondered, as he had an idea what made Elder Sun leave.
After leaving the Immortal Sun Peak, Yuan wandered the Inner Court to see if any of the disciples were gossiping, and they did not disappoint.
"Did you hear?
All nine Immortal Clans gathered for a meeting for the first time in decades."
"If the Nine Immortal Clan suddenly became active, something big will surely happen soon."
Hearing this information, Yuan realized the Nine Immortal Clans were planning on sealing the Desolate Continent with the Immortal Ensnaring Vault.
This meant that Elder Sun's sudden departure was most likely because the life-saving treasure she had secretly given Tian Yang had been activated, signaling that he was in danger.
'At this rate, the opening of Han Zexian's Tomb will happen in about a year...'
A few days later, Elder Sun returned.
"Sorry for suddenly leaving you like that," she apologized to him.
"There's no need to apologize.
That said, I'm curious.
Did something happen?" Yuan knew it was unlikely Elder Sun would tell him about the situation, but he still asked.
To his surprise, Elder Sun said with a deep sigh, "I gave Tian Yang a life-saving treasure before he left the sect, and I sensed its activation.
I don't know what he's gotten himself into this time, but he's likely in a life-or-death situation."
"That doesn't sound good.
Are you going to leave the sect to save him?"
Elder Sun shook her head.
"Unfortunately, I don't know where he is right now.
I am only able to sense the activation of the treasure, not where it was activated from..."
Yuan fell silent for a moment before speaking, "Have you heard of a place called the Desolate Continent?"
"The Desolate Continent?
Of course, it's a lawless place.
Why did you bring it up?"
"Well, to be honest, I heard a few of the disciples talking about Tian Yang visiting that place."
"What?!
Is that true?!" Elder Sun's eyes widened with disbelief.
Yuan calmly nodded.
"That dumb, stupid idiot!" Elder Sun stomped the ground angrily, her face full of frustration.
"Of all places, why'd he go there?!"
"Now that you know where he is, are you going to help him?" Yuan then asked.
"That's...
Even if I know where he is, I need to ask the Sect Leader for permission first."
"If you're going to speak with the Sect Leader, can you bring me with you?
I'd like to speak with him, too."
"What?
The Sect Leader isn't someone you can meet just because you want to."
"I know, but it won't hurt to ask.
After all, I've already spoken to him once before."
"Okay, I'll ask him.
I will let you know when he responds."
Yuan nodded.
A week later, Elder Sun revealed the Sect Leader's response to Yuan, "The Sect Leader has agreed to speak with you, but he said it'd cost you 1,000,000 points, whatever that means."
'A million points just to speak with him?
That's robbery in broad daylight!' Yuan cried inwardly after hearing this.
"Okay..." He nodded.
"Then I'll bring you to speak with him in three days."
Three days later, Elder Sun and Yuan made their way to the Sect Leader's quarters.
"Wait here while I speak with the Sect Leader first," Elder Sun said to Yuan before entering the building.
Her conversation with the Sect Leader lasted only for a few minutes.
"Did you get the Sect Leader's permission to leave the sect?" Yuan asked her.
"Yes.
It's your turn now.
I'll wait for you."
"I'll be back."
A few moments later, Yuan entered the Sect Leader's room.
"It's you again." The Sect Leader frowned upon seeing Yuan's face.
Of course, it wasn't because he disliked Yuan.
It was just a natural reaction for the Sect Leader.
"What do you want?
A million points will only grant you ten minutes with me."
"I have a few questions," Yuan quickly responded.
"In that case, it'll cost you an additional 100,000 points for every question."
Yuan was left speechless after hearing this, but as much as he wanted to complain, he had no qualifications to do so, as this was not his world or trial.
'After paying 1,000,000 points, I have 300,000 points left...
Three questions, huh?
Better make them count...' he sighed inwardly.
After a moment of silence, Yuan spoke, "For my first question, I want to know how I can leave the sect.
I want to visit the Desolate Continent with Elder Sun."
The Sect Leader smiled and said, "Instead of asking if you can leave, you asked for the method, huh?"
"If you wish to leave the Immortal Monastery and start venturing outside, you must pay a one-time fee of 10,000,000 points."
Yuan's eyes widened at the astronomical amount.
"Ten million points just to leave?!" he was in disbelief.

chapters.title: Chapter 1897 The Requirements to Pass the Trial
paragraphs: "I know you can create whatever rules you want, but isn't 10,000,000 points asking for too much? One can get several powerful treasures with that many points." Yuan tried to convince the Sect Leader to be reasonable.
However, the Sect Leader remained firm on his price and said, "Ten million points. I won't accept a single point less."

Yuan then said, "How about this? I am willing to pay 10,000,000 points, but can I pay you later? I want to follow Elder Sun to the Desolate Continent, but I need at least half a year to collect that many points."

The Sect Leader did not immediately respond. After a moment of silence, he finally spoke, "Since I know you're more than capable of collecting that many points, I'm willing to delay your payment for one year. However, for every year you fail to pay me, I will add another ten million points to your debt. If you fail to pay me back within 4 years, I will disqualify you from the trial. What do you think?"
Yuan immediately nodded, "I accept."
"Very well. Any more questions?"
Yuan then asked his second question, "How do we complete the trial? What is our actual goal? Because right now, it isn't clear what we're actually supposed to do here."

In response, the Sect Leader raised three fingers and said, "In order to complete the trial, you must achieve three things. One, accumulate a hundred million points. The points you have already spent still count. Two, become a Core Disciple. Last but not least, fully master the Peerless Immortal Technique. The first one to achieve these three goals will inherit my legacy. Simple enough, right?"

Yuan could only sigh inwardly at the sheer audacity of these goals. Though they appeared simple and straightforward on the surface, they were anything but. Each would demand an immense amount of time and effort, especially the last one, which might require one's lifetime to accomplish.

In order to acquire a hundred million points, one would need to spend at least 50 months inside the center region of the Hunting Grounds while hunting at Yuan's pace, as he would acquire about 2 million points a month if he spent all of his time hunting magical beasts.

Becoming a Core Disciple was no simple feat either. It required not only the accumulation of 1,000 contribution points but also reaching the esteemed realm of Spirit Enlightenment—a milestone that, for those without the Heaven Refining Physique, would take decades of relentless cultivation to achieve.

Yet, even these arduous requirements paled in comparison to the final trial, which was simply outrageous. In all of history, only a single individual had ever perfected the Peerless Immortal Technique—the founder of the Immortal Monastery himself. Compared to such an impossible feat, the other requirements were mere child's play, like pebbles before a towering mountain.

"Do you really expect one of us to perfect the Peerless Immortal Technique?" Yuan said. "If you didn't want anyone to inherit your legacy, you could've just said so. Instead, you're making us chase after a near-impossible goal without even telling us about it. If I hadn't spent 100,000 points to ask a question, who knows how long it would've taken us to realize the goal."
Instead of taking offense at Yuan's words, the Sect Leader's lips curled into a wide grin, his gaze unwavering as he spoke with absolute conviction.

"So what if it takes a long time? Even if it requires millions of years to complete, I will not lower the goals. This is the bare minimum I expect from the one who dares to inherit my legacy. If you lack the patience, then leave—no one is forcing you to partake in this trial."
He paused for a moment before adding, "Besides, time flows much slower in this world. No matter how long you spend here, the outside world will barely notice your absence."
"How long has passed in the real world?" Yuan then asked.
"I consider that a question, so it'll cost you 100,000 points if you want an answer," the Sect Leader warned him.
"I still want to know," Yuan answered without hesitation.
The Sect Leader then responded, "Although you've spent a few years in this world, only four months have passed in your world."
"Only four months?" Yuan was quite surprised to learn this information.
"Alright, your ten minutes is up. If you want to continue our conversation, come back with another million points—after you return your debt."
Before Yuan could even respond, the Sect Leader waved his sleeves, teleporting Yuan outside.
"Oh? When did you come out?" Yuan's sudden appearance startled Elder Sun a little.
"Just now."
"I see. What did you talk to the Sect Leader about, if you don't mind me asking?"
"I don't mind. I basically asked him to let me leave the sect to follow you."
"What?! Why would you want to follow me?! I'm not leaving the sect to play!" Elder Sun was baffled to hear that Yuan wanted to follow her to the Desolate Continent.
"I am well aware. However, I have always been interested in the Desolate Continent, and I saw this as a chance to fulfill my dream of going there."

Elder Sun rubbed her eyes and sighed, "No, I cannot let you follow me to such a dangerous place. You may be a genius, but you're still only a Spirit Grandmaster, not to mention your lack of experience in the outside world."
"It may be dangerous, but I am not worried at all because I know you will protect me, Elder Sun," Yuan said with a beaming smile, leaving her speechless.
"Just how thick is your skin? Do you even know what the meaning of shame is?"
Yuan shrugged and said, "Regardless, I already received the Sect Leader's permission. If you won't bring me with you, I'll just have to go alone."

"Y-You stubborn brat! Why can't you just listen to me, your master, for once?! You're just as reckless and stubborn as Tian Yang! No... you're even worse than him!" Elder Sun shouted at him, her fists clenched tightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1898 Leaving the Immortal Monastery
paragraphs: "Elder Sun, I am serious. I want to go with you to the Desolate Continent. You have no idea how much I sacrificed to get the Sect Leader's approval," Yuan said with a serious expression on his face.

Elder Sun sighed, "Whatever. You'll go by yourself if I refuse anyway, so I might as well bring you with me. You'll be a little safer that way. Promise me you'll not leave my side for as long as we're there."
"I promise," Yuan nodded.
"Come to the Immortal Sun Peak in three days. We'll leave then," she said a moment later.
After leaving, Yuan went to meet up with the others to let them know about his absence.
"What? You can leave the sect?" Ji Ran was shocked to learn this.
"Yes, but it'll cost you ten million points."
"Ten million?! That's straight-up robbery!" Xi Meili exclaimed.
"Do you think we'll be able to acquire points outside the sect? Otherwise, I cannot justify spending so many points..." Lan Yingying asked.
"I don't know, but we might be able to sell whatever we acquired outside to the stores for points once we get back to the sect," Yuan speculated.
"How long will you be gone for?" Yingzi asked.
"I don't know, but I have four years to repay my debt, so I doubt I'll be out for too long."
Yuan then told the others about paying for an audience with the Sect Leader and their true goal.
"Although it may seem expensive at first, I think it's worth it, as this may be the only way for us to get any answers."
"But these requirements... How long do you think it'll take one to complete them?" Xi Meili asked.

Ji Ran responded with a solemn expression, "Acquiring a hundred million points and becoming a Core Disciple will take a few decades, but to achieve level 9 in the Peerless Immortal Technique... I'm not sure if that's even possible."
"What level did you reach when you were the Sect Leader? And how long did it take?" Yuan asked.
"I only reached the peak of the 7th level, which took me almost three million years to achieve."

"Three million years?! There's no way I'm willing to spend even a tenth of that much time here! Even if time passes slower in this world, it won't matter since we'd still need to spend that much time in here!" Xi Meili exclaimed, her motivation to continue this trial dropping significantly.

"Three million years?! There's no way I'm willing to spend even a tenth of that much time here! Even if time passes slower in this world, it won't matter since we'd still need to spend that much time in here!" Xi Meili exclaimed, her motivation to continue this trial dropping significantly.
"Looks like this trial is much more complicated and time-consuming than we all thought. What are you going to do now? Are you going to continue?" Lan Yingying looked at Yuan.
"Honestly? I don't think I will complete this trial. I will probably give up sooner or later." Yuan said.

He'd already thought about giving up before even his conversation with the Sect Leader was over. This trial was simply too time-consuming. Moreover, the reward for the trial wasn't enticing to Yuan, who already knew most of their techniques and secrets.
"When will you leave? I'll stay in here until you leave," Xi Meili said.
"Probably after I return from this little trip," he said.
Yuan then looked at Ji Ran and asked him, "What about you? Will you stay here? Since time flows differently in here, you can stay here while we leave."
"That's..." Ji Ran couldn't give an immediate answer. He wanted to stay, but he had to follow Yuan.
Yuan could guess what he was thinking and said, "I don't mind if you stay here."
"Please give me some time to think about it," Ji Ran eventually said.
Yuan nodded.
Three days later, Yuan met with Elder Sun at Immortal Sun Peak.
"Are you ready to leave?" she asked him.
"Yes, I am ready."

Elder Sun swiftly retrieved a flying treasure, and to Yuan's surprise, it took the form of a majestic white lion. Its pristine fur shimmered like polished jade, and roaring flames engulfed its powerful legs, crackling with an otherworldly brilliance. The beast radiated an aura of dominance and grace, exuding an ancient power that seemed to shake the very air around it.
This was Yuan's first time seeing Elder Sun's flying treasure, and it looked even more realistic than the one Kulas had.
"That looks expensive," Yuan said out loud.
"What flying treasure isn't expensive?"
Yuan smiled and said, "More than what a sect elder should be able to afford. Now that I think about it, I know nothing of your background, Elder Sun."
Elder Sun sighed and said, "Stop being a busybody and get on it, or I will leave you behind."
Elder Sun leaped onto the back of the majestic flying treasure, treating it as effortlessly as one would a common steed. Without hesitation, Yuan followed suit, landing just behind her.

Before he could utter a single word, the white lion let out a low, rumbling growl, and in the blink of an eye, it ascended into the sky. Flames flickered from its legs as it propelled itself upward, piercing through the clouds with breathtaking speed. The world below blurred into insignificance, swallowed by the vast expanse of the heavens.
Yuan gazed at the endless sky stretching before them and asked, "How long do you think it'll take to reach the Desolate Continent?"
Despite their extreme speed, he felt only a gentle breeze brushing against his face.
"We should arrive in a week," she calmly replied.
'A week?! That's too fast!' Yuan cried inwardly.

"Since we have some time, why don't you tell me a little about yourself? When you asked me about my background, I realized that I also didn't know anything about you," Elder Sun said, being a busybody herself.
Yuan smiled and said, "I came from a place called Earth."
"Earth? I've never heard of this place before."
"It's a small and insignificant place, so I'm not surprised."
"Why did you join the Immortal Monastery?"
"The same reason why most people do—to change my life."
Elder Sun continued to question Yuan for the next several hours.

chapters.title: Chapter 1899 Visiting the Desolate Continent
paragraphs: "Elder Sun, it's unfair that I'm the only one answering your questions. Let me ask you a few questions, as well," Yuan eventually said.
Elder Sun narrowed her eyes, clearly hesitant to have her background questioned.
'Since he is my first disciple...'
A moment later, she nodded, "Alright, you can ask me a few questions. However, you can't ask anything too personal."
"Then I will ask you questions that you've already asked me."
Yuan then asked, "Why did you join the Immortal Monastery?"

Elder Sun pondered for a bit before responding, "I joined the Immortal Monastery to escape my family. While it's not like I am running away from home, I just wanted to be away from them. The atmosphere is too suffocating for my taste."
"I see... then how long have you been at the Immortal Monastery? Did you start as a disciple?"
Knowing she most likely wouldn't answer, Yuan avoided asking about Elder Sun's family situation.
"I think I've been working at the Immortal Monastery for about half a century now. I was already qualified as a sect elder, so I went straight for that position."
"Half a century? How old are you?"
"You should never ask a young lady their age." Elder Sun sneered.
"Right... then where are you from?"
Elder Sun hesitated at this question, but she eventually answered, "The Holy Continent."
"What? The Holy Continent?" Yuan's eyes widened with surprise.

During the Primordial Era, there existed a revered land known as the Holy Continent, and it possessed the highest density of spiritual energy in all of the Divine Heaven. The very air shimmered with qi, and the land pulsed with boundless vitality, making it the ultimate haven for cultivation.

Such a paradise inevitably drew countless cultivators. However, entry was not a privilege granted to all. Only those from the most prestigious and powerful backgrounds, such as the Nine Immortal Clans, were permitted to set foot within its sacred grounds. To the rest of the world, the Holy Continent remained a distant dream, an untouchable utopia reserved for the chosen few.
"You must come from an extremely powerful family..." Yuan mumbled.
"Don't tell me... you're from the Nine Immortal Clans?" he swallowed nervously.
Elder Sun raised an eyebrow and said, "No, I am not from the Nine Immortal Clans. Do you have any grievances with them? It's subtle, but I can sense it in your tone."
"Something like that, I guess."

"This should be common sense, but you shouldn't mess with the Nine Immortal Clans. While they are influential, that's not the main reason. The Nine Immortal Clans are a vengeful bunch. Nothing good comes from messing with them."
Yuan smiled and said, "Don't worry, my issue with the Nine Immortal Clans was resolved long ago."
Yuan continued to ask Elder Sun questions. Since he had yet to fully regain Tian Yang's memories, he didn't have much information on her.
A week passed in the blink of an eye, and they arrived at their destination—the Desolate Continent.
"So, do you have any idea on how to find him?" Yuan asked Elder Sun.
"No... And as much as I want to just wander around, the Desolate Continent is massive. It'd take months if we searched randomly."
Yuan pondered for a moment before speaking, "How about we visit the Southern Stronghold first?"
"Why? Did Tian Yang mention where he was going to the other disciples?" Elder Sun asked.
"No, it's just a guess." Yuan shook his head.

However, according to his memories, Tian Yang should currently be in the Southern Stronghold, accompanying Huang Xiao Li in her search for her missing family. "Alright. Now we just need to find the Southern Stronghold," Elder Sun nodded.
Since this was her first time visiting the Desolate Continent, Elder Sun had no idea where anything was. Fortunately, she came prepared and brought a map with her.
"The Southern Stronghold should be in that direction." Yuan pointed in a certain direction.
Elder Sun looked at him with raised eyebrows.
"How do you know? Have you been here before?"
Yuan shook his head, "No, but I have studied a lot about it. After all, I have always wanted to visit this place."
"Is that so?" Elder Sun didn't question him further and controlled the flying treasure to head toward the Southern Stronghold.
Sometime later, Elder Sun landed her flying treasure right outside the Southern Stronghold's gate, instantly attracting many gazes.
After putting away the flying treasure, Elder Sun and Yuan entered the city to look for Tian Yang.
A few hours into their search, Elder Sun suddenly spoke to Yuan using voice transmission, "We're being followed."
Yuan smiled and calmly responded, "I'm not surprised. You were essentially asking to be robbed by showing off your flying treasure."
"Showing off...? I did no such thing..."
"If it's out in the open, you're showing off—at least that's how things work within the Desolate Continent. Are you going to kill them?"
"If they try anything funny."
A day quickly passed, but they were still unable to find Tian Yang despite Elder Sun using divine sense the entire time.
"Looks like he isn't in this city," Elder Sun said.
'Did they already go to the Western Stronghold?' Yuan wondered inwardly.
"Let's try the Western Stronghold this time," he suggested a moment later.
"Alright."
Without lingering, the two of them quickly made their way to the Western Stronghold. Not wanting to waste money on the Teleportation Arrays, Elder Sun continued using her flying treasure.

However, the moment they left the city, a decently sized group of over a hundred individuals ambushed them, encircling them like a pack of hungry beasts. Their gazes burned with ill intent, their weapons gleaming under the light.
The air grew heavy with murderous intent as one of them shouted, "If you want to live, hand over all of your treasures!"
Yuan silently looked at Elder Sun and wondered how she was going to react.
"What the hell is that?" the group muttered in unison, their voices tinged with confusion and unease as they lifted their heads to stare at the hovering golden wheel.

Before they could even begin to comprehend its powers, the wheel began spinning, its speed blurring its intricate engravings into streaks of light. Then, as if ignited by an unseen force, it erupted into golden flames, radiating an overwhelming pressure that made the air itself tremble.

A moment later, without warning, a golden firestorm descended upon the bandits like the wrath of a celestial deity. Screams barely had time to form before they were silenced—their bodies consumed in an instant, reduced to nothing but ashes.
